## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Dutiyakaraṇīyavimānavatthu* ("Second Should-Be-Done Mansion", Vv 57) is a canonical verse text belonging to the *Vimānavatthu* collection [SuttaCentral]. The core theme of the discourse centers on the teaching that having confidence in Buddhist monastics is sufficient to yield immense spiritual and heavenly reward [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral catalogs four modern translations of the text across four languages [SuttaCentral].
Exegesis of the text is preserved in the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, which reproduces and explains the verses across segments 1.1–8.1 [DharmaNexus]. While SuttaCentral records no cross-language parallels and DharmaNexus detects no significant matches outside Pali, DharmaNexus identifies 140 matching passages across seventeen Pali canonical and paracanonical texts [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. The discourse shares virtually its entire poetic structure (§0.1–8.1) with its immediate predecessor, the *Paṭhamakaraṇīyavimānavatthu* (Vv 56), alongside extensive formulaic and verse overlap with other poems in the collection, including the *Guttilavimānavatthu* (Vv 33), *Dvārapālavimānavatthu* (Vv 55), *Caturitthivimānavatthu* (Vv 45), and *Dutiyasūcivimānavatthu* (Vv 59) [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
